complexity.notes: Correct for both parities; the termination logic (a+1 < b vs else-break, plus the a == b cleanup) is a bit fiddly — a cleaner loop condition could avoid the break, but this is just style. The O(n) extra array can be eliminated entirely: ||find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then interleave the two halves|| achieves O(1) space with the same O(n) time. The `if not head` guard is dead code under the stated constraints (length >= 1) but harmless.
complexity.summary: Collects all nodes into an array, then walks two indices from both ends, rewiring each front node to point at its mirrored back node and the back node at the next front node until the pointers meet. Handles odd and even lengths with separate termination cases.
